title: Talking About What Would Have Happened
goal: Use skulle, ville, burde, and kunne ha plus a past participle to describe unreal past outcomes, regrets, missed obligations, and possibilities.

objectives.statement: Use skulle, ville, burde, and kunne ha plus a past participle to describe unreal past outcomes, regrets, missed obligations, and possibilities.

sections.title: A dinner that did not go as planned

spans.value: Mina has invited several friends to dinner. Her brother, Jonas, promised to help, but delays and misunderstandings have left them with too little food and no dessert.
Du skulle ha kommet klokka fem.

blocks.translation: You were supposed to come at five.

blocks.translation: I know. I should have sent you a message.

spans.value: Da kunne jeg ha bedt Nora om hjelp.

blocks.translation: Then I could have asked Nora for help.

spans.value: Jeg ville ha kommet tidligere, men toget ble innstilt.

blocks.translation: I would have come earlier, but the train was cancelled.

spans.value: Og du skulle ha kjøpt brød.

blocks.translation: And you were supposed to buy bread.

spans.value: Ja. Jeg kunne ha kjøpt det på stasjonen, men jeg tenkte ikke på det.

blocks.translation: Yes. I could have bought it at the station, but I didn’t think of it.

spans.value: Vi burde ha planlagt dette bedre.

blocks.translation: We should have planned this better.

spans.value: Hvis jeg hadde visst at toget var innstilt, ville jeg ha tatt bussen.

blocks.translation: If I had known that the train was cancelled, I would have taken the bus.

spans.value: The dinner has not started yet, but Mina and Jonas are looking backward. In this failed-plan context, they present actions as expected, advisable, possible but unrealized, or dependent on a different past situation. The dialogue establishes which actions did not occur or were not completed as intended.
skulle, ville, burde, or kunne + ha + past participle
A past participle (perfektum partisipp) is the verb form already used after

no.value: Jonas har kjøpt brød.

en.value: Jonas has bought bread.

no.value: Jonas skulle ha kjøpt brød.

en.value: Jonas was supposed to buy bread.

spans.value: is the finite verb and is followed by the infinitive

These forms concern past actions or outcomes. This lesson combines each modal with failed-plan context to practice a particular past perspective. The context establishes nonfulfillment or nonoccurrence; the modal marks how the speaker presents the past.

items.value: an earlier plan, arrangement, duty, or expectation that the context establishes was not fulfilled
an unreal past outcome or intended response under different circumstances
retrospective advice, criticism, or regret about a contextually established omission or inadequate action
a past possibility or opportunity that the context establishes was not realized

spans.value: The forms overlap in some situations, but these target readings do not present the failed past from the same perspective.

sections.title: Unfulfilled plans and expectations: skulle ha

spans.value: In the failed-plan reading taught here, use
to present something as planned, arranged, promised, or expected. Surrounding context establishes that it did not happen as intended.

no.value: Jonas skulle ha kommet klokka fem.

en.value: Jonas was supposed to come at five.

no.value: Han skulle ha kjøpt brød.

en.value: He was supposed to buy bread.

no.value: Nora skulle ha laget dessert.

en.value: Nora was supposed to make dessert.

spans.value: These sentences look back at an earlier arrangement. In context, Jonas did not arrive at five, he did not buy bread, and Nora did not make dessert.
can also express an intention that was not carried out:

no.value: Jeg skulle ha ringt deg, men mobilen var tom for strøm.

en.value: I was going to call you, but my phone was out of power.

no.value: Vi skulle ha bestilt bord, men vi glemte det.

en.value: We were going to reserve a table, but we forgot.

spans.value: The compact rule for this lesson is:

statement.value: Use skulle ha to present the earlier plan or expectation; use the failed-plan context to establish that it was not fulfilled.

sections.title: Skulle ha and burde ha are not identical

spans.value: can sometimes tempt learners to use
everywhere. Norwegian usually separates an earlier arrangement from a later judgment.

no.value: Jeg skulle ha møtt henne klokka seks.

en.value: I was supposed to meet her at six.

no.value: Jeg burde ha møtt henne tidligere.

en.value: I should have met her earlier.

spans.value: This evaluates the past and says that meeting her earlier would have been better.
In Mina’s complaint, the arrangement is central:

no.value: Du skulle ha kommet klokka fem.

en.value: You were supposed to come at five.

no.value: Du burde ha kommet tidligere.

en.value: You should have come earlier.

spans.value: she is giving retrospective criticism or advice. There may have been no fixed arrangement for five o’clock.
for an outcome that would have happened under different circumstances.

no.value: Hvis jeg hadde visst at toget var innstilt, ville jeg ha tatt bussen.

en.value: If I had known that the train was cancelled, I would have taken the bus.

spans.value: He did not know, so he did not take the bus.

no.value: Uten forsinkelsen ville han ha kommet i tide.

en.value: Without the delay, he would have arrived on time.

no.value: Med mer mat ville gjestene ha blitt lenger.

en.value: With more food, the guests would have stayed longer.

no.value: Jeg ville ha hjulpet deg hvis jeg hadde vært hjemme.

en.value: I would have helped you if I had been at home.

spans.value: The condition does not always need to be stated. Shared context can make it clear:

no.value: Jeg ville ha sagt ja, men jeg fikk aldri spørsmålet.

en.value: I would have said yes, but I was never asked.

no.value: Det ville ha vært hyggelig.

en.value: That would have been nice.

statement.value: Use ville ha when the important fact is an unreal past result: what would have happened in different circumstances.

sections.title: Do not replace ville with skulle automatically

spans.value: in some contexts, learners may treat them as interchangeable. In this lesson’s past-looking pattern, keep the central contrast clear:

no.value: Jonas skulle ha tatt bussen klokka fire.

en.value: Jonas was supposed to take the bus at four.

spans.value: There was a plan or expectation.

no.value: Jonas ville ha tatt bussen hvis han hadde visst om problemet.

en.value: Jonas would have taken the bus if he had known about the problem.

spans.value: Taking the bus was an unreal result dependent on different knowledge.

sections.title: Regret, advice, and criticism: burde ha

spans.value: to say that a past action would have been better, wiser, safer, or more appropriate. It often communicates regret or criticism.

no.value: Jeg burde ha sendt deg en melding.

en.value: I should have sent you a message.

no.value: Vi burde ha planlagt dette bedre.

en.value: We should have planned this better.

no.value: Du burde ha sjekket rutetidene.

en.value: You should have checked the timetable.

no.value: De burde ha bestilt mer mat.

en.value: They should have ordered more food.

spans.value: In this lesson’s scenarios, context establishes that the action did not happen or did not happen adequately.

no.value: Jeg burde ha lyttet til deg.

en.value: I should have listened to you.

no.value: Vi burde ha reist tidligere.

en.value: We should have left earlier.

spans.value: or another person, it may sound like criticism:

no.value: Du burde ha sagt fra.

en.value: You should have let us know.

spans.value: Context and tone determine how strong that criticism feels.
The compact rule for this lesson is:

statement.value: Use burde ha for retrospective judgment that a different or better past action was preferable; context establishes what actually happened.

no.value: Jeg burde ikke ha ventet så lenge.

en.value: I should not have waited so long.

no.value: Vi burde ikke ha invitert så mange.

en.value: We should not have invited so many people.

spans.value: The regret now concerns an action that did happen but should not have happened.
Compare these readings in contexts that establish what happened:

no.value: Jeg burde ha ringt.

en.value: I should have called.

spans.value: The context establishes that the desired action did not happen.

no.value: Jeg burde ikke ha ringt så sent.

en.value: I should not have called so late.

spans.value: The context establishes that the call happened, and the speaker now judges it negatively.
In the missed-possibility reading taught here, use
to present an action or outcome as possible in the past. Surrounding context establishes that it did not become reality.

no.value: Jeg kunne ha bedt Nora om hjelp.

en.value: I could have asked Nora for help.

no.value: Jonas kunne ha kjøpt brød på stasjonen.

en.value: Jonas could have bought bread at the station.

no.value: De kunne ha bestilt pizza.

en.value: They could have ordered pizza.

no.value: Vi kunne ha spist ute.

en.value: We could have eaten out.

spans.value: These sentences do not necessarily say that the action was required or advisable. They identify an available possibility, while the dinner context establishes that it was not used.

no.value: Jonas skulle ha kjøpt brød.

en.value: Jonas was supposed to buy bread.

no.value: Jonas burde ha kjøpt brød.

en.value: Jonas should have bought bread.

spans.value: The speaker now thinks buying bread would have been the better choice.

no.value: Jonas kunne ha kjøpt brød.

en.value: Jonas could have bought bread.

spans.value: Buying bread was possible; the dinner context establishes that he did not do it.
The compact rule for this lesson is:

statement.value: Use kunne ha to present a past possibility or opportunity; use context to establish that it was not realized.

spans.value: refers to a possible outcome rather than a deliberate choice:

no.value: Det kunne ha gått galt.

en.value: It could have gone wrong.

no.value: Toget kunne ha kommet enda senere.

en.value: The train could have arrived even later.

sections.title: Changed situation: after a missed appointment

spans.value: The next day, Jonas misses an appointment at a bicycle repair shop. The shop had reserved a time for him, his phone was working, a later bus was available, and he now realizes that leaving home earlier would have prevented the problem.
Without looking back, complete one line for each perspective: the failed arrangement, the unreal outcome, the regret, and the unused option.
